# hallpass_git_remote (Resource)

A git host (GitHub, GitLab, your own server) agents clone from and push to with plain git through the gateway. Pin its host keys with `hallpass_host_key` and add `hallpass_git_access_profile`s. The alias is the first part of every repository path agents use (`git clone center:<alias>/<owner>/<repo>.git`). Destroying it deletes the remote and its profiles. Import with the server ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hallpass_git_remote" "github" {
  alias       = "github"
  description = "GitHub (acme organization)"
  address     = "github.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `address` (String) Host name of the git host, e.g. `github.com`. Its SSH address ranges must be inside the gateway's `egress.allow_cidrs`.
- `alias` (String) Unique name agents use. Gateway command words are reserved.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description, shown to operators.
- `display_name` (String) Display name (defaults to the alias).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the git remote is enabled. Disabling ends active access within seconds and cancels pending requests; enabling lets policy decide again.
- `groups` (Set of String) Groups of the git remote, used by policy selectors.
- `labels` (Map of String) Labels of the git remote, used by policy selectors.
- `port` (Number) SSH port.

### Read-Only

- `environment` (String) Always empty for git remotes.
- `id` (String) Server ID (`srv_…`).
- `metadata` (Map of String) Always empty for git remotes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Server ID
terraform import hallpass_git_remote.github srv_01m5qh1t09e4jbmeys0q0bjz8j
```
